questions.question: For a prompt containing an 80-page policy and one question, what ordering is recommended?
options: Question first, then the document, so the model knows what to look for
Document first, then the instructions and question at the end
Split the question into halves placed before and after the document
Order does not matter for long documents
questions.explanation: For long inputs, placing documents at the top and the question at the end tends to produce better answers.

questions.question: What does the context window have to hold?
options: Only the documents you paste in
The system prompt, documents, conversation so far, and the response being generated
questions.explanation: Everything the model considers and produces counts against the context window, so you must leave room for the output.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of asking the model to extract relevant quotes before answering?
options: It grounds the answer in the source text and gives you an audit trail to check
It lets the model use knowledge outside the documents
It removes the need for any human review
questions.explanation: Quote-then-answer focuses the model on relevant passages and lets you verify each quote against the original quickly.

questions.question: In map-reduce summarisation of a document larger than the context window, what happens in the "reduce" step?
options: The document is compressed into a zip file
Each chunk is summarised with a different prompt
The per-chunk outputs are merged, de-duplicated, and summarised in a final prompt
The least relevant chunks are deleted without being read
questions.explanation: Map runs the same prompt on each chunk; reduce combines those outputs into a single result, ideally keeping each chunk's location for citations.
